Dimitri Khundadze - Peace is the only necessary condition that will support economic development; Georgia is moving in the right direction with its improvisational policy  
12:17, 10.04.2026

Peace is the only necessary condition that will support economic development, – this was stated by Dimitri Khundadze, Secretary General of “People’s Power.”

Speaking about Georgia’s role as one of the key players in the Middle Corridor, Dimitri Khundadze noted that the country’s economic development will preserve Georgia’s function as a regional leader.

According to him, this can only be achieved in conditions of peace, because war and development are incompatible.

“Peace is the necessary condition for using the country’s transport capabilities. A few days ago, when the situation in the Middle East became extremely tense, only Georgia’s airspace was congested on the transport and aviation map. This was a very small example of the big picture I am talking about: peace is a necessary condition for fulfilling a transit function.

How can a country join sanctions when it will not gain any result from this, even for the customer? How do you imagine destroying Russia’s economy with Georgian sanctions? Our opponents raise the issue that active steps must be taken to improve the social situation, pensions and salaries must be increased, jobs must be created, tourism must be developed, and so on. They present their proposals directly in figures. For example, representatives of Gakharia’s party introduced an initiative that the minimum wage should be 1,050 lari. “Lelo” raises the issue that pensions should be increased to 1,000 lari, and all this should happen against the backdrop of sanctions? In wartime, isn’t that unimaginable?!

These are hypocritically noble statements. Some people sometimes let slip that it is better for hot bombs to fall than for there to be peace in Georgia. Development and war — these two things are incompatible. Georgia, with its improvisational policy, is clearly moving in the right direction. By comparison, no one in Ukraine today is thinking about increasing pensions or building schools and kindergartens. In Ukraine, there is only one concern: somehow to save this or that family member. More than 10 million people have already become displaced, and the economy has been destroyed.

Here, however, tourism figures have increased over the past year. It was 4.4 billion in 2024, and 4.7 was recorded in 2025. Investments are growing, and the country’s economy has grown to 100 billion. This is exactly where the opportunity lies to develop infrastructure, attract investments, and bring in even more tourists. Then it will become possible to increase pensions more quickly and create jobs more intensively — in recent times, the number has increased by 40,000. I am not saying that everything is ideal; I am saying that in this extremely difficult period, with such a policy we not only preserved peace and avoided war, but also managed to improve in every direction compared to yesterday. However, that is not enough, and we want even better,” said Dimitri Khundadze.
